description: Chord recogniser: it names the chord arriving on its polyphonic pitch input, draws it in standard notation and puts the chord's root out as a pitch

params.text: Sets the root of the key signature the notation is written in, and leans the spelling of note and chord names towards that key; chord recognition is not changed by it
Sets the mode of the key signature the notation is written in, one of the seven diatonic modes; chord recognition is not changed by it

inputs.text: The notes to identify, at 1V per octave, one per channel of a polyphonic cable; the octave a note is in and any doubling of it make no difference to the chord that is named
Restricts the reading to those pitch channels whose gate here is above 5V; unpatched, every channel of the pitch input is read
Sets the key signature from a twelve-channel Poly External Scale cable: under 4V a note outside the scale, under 9V a note in it, above that the root

outputs.text: The key signature as a twelve-channel Poly External Scale cable: 0V for a note outside it, 8V for a note in it and 10V for the root
The root of the recognised chord at 1V per octave, holding the last root it found while the input is not a chord it recognises
10V while the input is a recognised chord, 0V when it is not

notes: the chords recognised are the major, minor, diminished, augmented, sus2 and sus4 triads, four sevenths and four ninths, each in any inversion; anything else is named as unrecognised
the staff and the chord name are a display; nothing has to be patched to the outputs for them to work
the red lamp beside the PES input lights when that cable has fewer than twelve channels or carries a scale the module does not recognise

inputs.1:
high above 5V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads every pitch channel read.

outputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
